comparable.host_disk: Amazon Elastic Block Store, non-rotational (kernel flag), nvme, ext4

durable.text:
# Fluent Bit 5.2.0, profile `durable` (its documented best for crash safety), for the
# spool comparison (#748). Each setting names its page under
# https://docs.fluentbit.io/manual/ (as published for 5.x).
#
# telemetry: Fluent Bit has no usage reporting; its HTTP monitoring server is off
# (administration/monitoring: `http_server`, stated here).
#
# What its cursor means, from its own docs: after an unexpected stop the tail
# input's guarantee is "at-least-once" and the offset database may trail the
# processed position (pipeline/inputs/tail "Keep state"); the S3 output buffers
# in `store_dir` and re-sends leftovers on restart, and states no formal
# delivery guarantee (pipeline/outputs/s3). A gap here is a measured consequence
# of when it moves its offset, shown beside these two settings.

[SERVICE]
    # administration/configuring-fluent-bit/classic-mode/configuration-file "flush"
    flush                     1
    log_level                 info
    http_server               off
    # administration/buffering-and-storage: chunks on the tool's own volume ...
    storage.path              /data/storage
    # ... synced with fsync on every write (`storage.sync full`, not the default `normal`).
    storage.sync              full
    storage.checksum          on

[INPUT]
    # pipeline/inputs/tail
    name                      tail
    tag                       spool
    # The active file and its rotated names, the same pattern every tool is given;
    # a renamed file is tracked by inode in the offset database
    # (pipeline/inputs/tail "File rotation").
    path                      /spool/file/app.log*,/spool/syslog-spool/app.log*
    # A backlog is read from its first byte, as every other tool reads it.
    read_from_head            true
    refresh_interval          1
    rotate_wait               30
    # pipeline/inputs/tail "Keep state": offsets in SQLite on the data volume,
    # synced fully (`db.sync full`; the default is `normal`).
    db                        /data/tail.db
    db.sync                   full
    db.locking                true
    # administration/buffering-and-storage: the input buffers on the filesystem.
    storage.type              filesystem
    mem_buf_limit             64MB

[OUTPUT]
    # pipeline/outputs/s3
    name                      s3
    match                     spool
    bucket                    bench
    region                    us-east-1
    # The lab MinIO (the S3 tap in crash cells).
    endpoint                  http://minio:9000
    # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object, gzip.
    total_file_size           32M
    upload_timeout            60s
    compression               gzip
    # One JSON line per record: the S3 output writes JSON lines by default.
    json_date_key             date
    # The S3 output's local buffer, on the tool's own volume.
    store_dir                 /data/s3
    # Whole objects with PutObject; ask the store to check a Content-MD5 (V1 in #744 (e)).
    use_put_object            on
    send_content_md5          on
    s3_key_format             /fluent-bit/%Y/%m/%d/%H%M%S-$UUID.gz
    retry_limit               no_limits

acks.text:
# Vector 0.61.0, profile `acks`, for the spool comparison (#748). Each setting names
# its page under https://vector.dev/docs/ (as published for 0.61).
#
# telemetry: Vector has no usage reporting; its API server is off
# (reference/api/: `api.enabled`, default false, stated here).

# reference/configuration/global-options/#data_dir: checkpoints and buffers on the tool's own volume.
data_dir: /var/lib/vector

api:
  enabled: false

sources:
  spool:
    # reference/configuration/sources/file/
    type: file
    # The active file and its rotated names, the same pattern every tool is given;
    # a renamed file keeps its fingerprint (below) and is not read twice
    # (sources/file/ "File rotation").
    include:
      - /spool/file/app.log*
      - /spool/syslog-spool/app.log*
    # A backlog is read from its first byte, as every other tool reads it.
    read_from: beginning
    # sources/file/#fingerprint: device and inode, so a copytruncate rotation's
    # truncated file is recognised as the same file and re-read from zero.
    fingerprint:
      strategy: device_and_inode
    # sources/file/#acknowledgements is deprecated in favour of the sink's setting below.

sinks:
  s3:
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/
    type: aws_s3
    inputs: [spool]
    bucket: bench
    key_prefix: "vector/%Y/%m/%d/"
    region: us-east-1
    # sinks/aws_s3/#endpoint: the lab MinIO (the S3 tap in crash cells).
    endpoint: http://minio:9000
    force_path_style: true
    # #744 rule 15: one JSON line per record, gzip at its default level.
    encoding:
      codec: json
    framing:
      method: newline_delimited
    compression: gzip
    # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object.
    batch:
      max_bytes: 33554432
      timeout_secs: 60
    # sinks/aws_s3/#request.concurrency: the default.
    request:
      concurrency: adaptive
    # reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/: the file checkpoint advances only
    # after this sink has delivered the event.
    acknowledgements:
      enabled: true
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/#buffer: a memory buffer that blocks
    # when full, so nothing is acknowledged before delivery.
    buffer:
      type: memory
      max_events: 10000
      when_full: block
    # Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the
    # container's environment (sinks/aws_s3/#auth, the default chain).

disk-buffer.text:
# Vector 0.61.0, profile `disk-buffer`, for the spool comparison (#748). Each setting names
# its page under https://vector.dev/docs/ (as published for 0.61).
#
# telemetry: Vector has no usage reporting; its API server is off
# (reference/api/: `api.enabled`, default false, stated here).

# reference/configuration/global-options/#data_dir: checkpoints and buffers on the tool's own volume.
data_dir: /var/lib/vector

api:
  enabled: false

sources:
  spool:
    # reference/configuration/sources/file/
    type: file
    # The active file and its rotated names, the same pattern every tool is given;
    # a renamed file keeps its fingerprint (below) and is not read twice
    # (sources/file/ "File rotation").
    include:
      - /spool/file/app.log*
      - /spool/syslog-spool/app.log*
    # A backlog is read from its first byte, as every other tool reads it.
    read_from: beginning
    # sources/file/#fingerprint: device and inode, so a copytruncate rotation's
    # truncated file is recognised as the same file and re-read from zero.
    fingerprint:
      strategy: device_and_inode
    # sources/file/#acknowledgements is deprecated in favour of the sink's setting below.

sinks:
  s3:
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/
    type: aws_s3
    inputs: [spool]
    bucket: bench
    key_prefix: "vector/%Y/%m/%d/"
    region: us-east-1
    # sinks/aws_s3/#endpoint: the lab MinIO (the S3 tap in crash cells).
    endpoint: http://minio:9000
    force_path_style: true
    # #744 rule 15: one JSON line per record, gzip at its default level.
    encoding:
      codec: json
    framing:
      method: newline_delimited
    compression: gzip
    # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object.
    batch:
      max_bytes: 33554432
      timeout_secs: 60
    # sinks/aws_s3/#request.concurrency: the default.
    request:
      concurrency: adaptive
    # reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/: the file checkpoint advances only
    # after this sink has delivered the event.
    acknowledgements:
      enabled: true
    # reference/configuration/sinks/aws_s3/#buffer: a disk buffer; with it an event is
    # acknowledged once it is in the buffer, which is synced every 500 ms
    # (reference/end-to-end-acknowledgements/). The documented durability trade.
    buffer:
      type: disk
      max_size: 1073741824
      when_full: block
    # Credentials come from AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY in the
    # container's environment (sinks/aws_s3/#auth, the default chain).

strong.text:
# VTOP, profile `strong` (the default commit rule), for the spool comparison (#748).
# Every setting names the page it comes from: docs/configure/reference.md (the
# reference for every config.yaml key) and examples/config.yaml at the commit
# under test.
#
# telemetry: VTOP has no usage reporting; OpenTelemetry export runs only when an
# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_*ENDPOINT is set, and the compose file sets
# OTEL_SDK_DISABLED=true (crates/vtop-observe/src/otel/settings.rs).

engine:
  name: spool-bench
  tenant: bench
  # docs/configure/reference.md "engine.state_store": SQLite on the tool's own data volume,
  # the same volume class as every other tool's state.
  state_store: "sqlite:///data/state/vtop-state.db"
  work_dir: /data/work
  work_retention_seconds: 86400
  work_max_bytes: 10737418240
  log_level: INFO

batching:
  # #744 rule 15: about 32 MiB or 60 s per object, whichever first; records unbounded.
  # docs/configure/reference.md "batching.max_bytes", "batching.max_batch_age_seconds".
  max_records: 100000000
  max_bytes: 33554432
  max_batch_age_seconds: 60
  # The shipped default (examples/config.yaml "max_concurrent_batches").
  max_concurrent_batches: 8

compression:
  # #744 rule 15: gzip at the tool's documented default level (examples/config.yaml
  # "compression": the code default is gzip level 6).
  type: gzip
  level: 6

sources:
  # docs/configure/reference.md "sources.file.paths" and "sources.syslog_spool.paths":
  # the active file and its rotated names (app.log.1, app.log.2, ...), the same
  # pattern every tool here is given: a backlog is written across rotated files
  # before the tool starts (#748 `drain`). A file renamed while it is being read
  # is followed by inode (crates/vtop-adapters/src/rotated.rs).
  # The generator writes one of the two directories per run (the `source` variant).
  file:
    enabled: true
    paths:
      - /spool/file/app.log*
  syslog_spool:
    enabled: true
    paths:
      - /spool/syslog-spool/app.log*

upload:
  # docs/configure/reference.md "upload": the native S3 backend against the lab MinIO.
  # In crash and fault cells `minio` resolves to the S3 tap, which forwards to the store.
  backend: s3_native
  bucket: bench
  prefix: "vtop/"
  endpoint_url: http://minio:9000
  region: us-east-1
  force_path_style: true
  # The lab store is plaintext (examples/config.yaml "verify_tls": the explicit lab opt-out).
  verify_tls: false
  create_bucket: true
  # The default: VERIFIED needs a digest derived from stored content.
  require_strong_verification: true

partitioning:
  template: "source={source}/format={format}/"

deviations: VTOP stores each line as read (newline-framed syslog, gzip); Vector and Fluent Bit wrap each line in a JSON object (their documented JSON output). The checker reads the id token in either form; object sizes and MiB/s are of SOURCE bytes, so the wrapping does not change them (rule 15).
Fluent Bit's S3 output has no byte-and-age pair identical to the others': `total_file_size 32M` and `upload_timeout 60s` are the closest documented settings.
Every tool reads the active file and its rotated names (`app.log*`): a backlog is written across rotated files before the tool starts. Rotated names are `app.log.<k>`, k never reused, never deleted.
Time to store-visible uses the generator's write time and MinIO's LastModified (milliseconds), both on the Docker VM's clock.

plan._comment: A GitHub-hosted runner (workflow_dispatch): crash-K1..K3, 9 kills per kind per tool, reduced backlog, 1 CPU per tool. Correctness only (#748 'Where it runs'); split from hosted-rotation so each fits one job. The backlog (about 300 MB) makes about nine 32 MiB objects per tool, so a trigger between the 1st and 3rd PUT of each life is reachable (review of #908).
